figureSources.source: Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the 1.25 MPI a curb weight of 1,110 kg, which ADAC's catalogue lists as 'Leergewicht (EU)', the EU mass in running order that includes a 75 kg driver; 75 kg is taken off to give 1,035 kg without a driver (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio (YB) an overall length of 4,065 mm (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio (YB) an overall width of 1,725 mm excluding mirrors (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio (YB) an overall height of 1,450 mm (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio (YB) a wheelbase of 2,580 mm (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio (YB) a front track of 1,518 mm on 15-inch wheels (rear 1,524 mm) (search snippet only, not opened).

No opened source: a search snippet citing NHTSA's measured inertial data puts passenger-car centre-of-gravity heights at about 0.50 to 0.58 m and compact cars at 500 to 560 mm; 0.53 m is the owner's choice inside that band until the NHTSA listing is opened.
auto motor und sport weighed a Kia Rio 1.0 T-GDI 120 GT-Line (same YB body, turbo engine, 2020 facelift) at 61.7 % front / 38.3 % rear (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification fits standard 185/65 R15 tyres; unloaded radius = (15 x 25.4 + 2 x 0.65 x 185) / 2 = 310.75 mm (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification and its Irish launch release give the Kia Rio (YB) a turning circle of 10.2 m; kerb-to-kerb wording not seen (search snippet only, not opened).
No source was found for wheel travel of a small hatchback (this page came up in the search and gives no figure); 0.15 m is the owner's choice, proposed, not sourced.

No opened source: a search snippet of OptimumG's Springs and Dampers Tech Tip 1 gives '0.5 - 1.5 Hz for passenger cars'; 1.2 Hz is the owner's choice inside that range until it is opened; Tech Tip 1 has only an http link, so the url given is Part Three of the same series.
No opened source: a search snippet of OptimumG's 'Of Springs and Dampers' puts passenger cars at about 0.3 when comfort is the priority; 0.3 is the owner's choice until the page is opened.

Worked out from ADAC's measured 35.5 m stop from 100 km/h for a Kia Rio 1.0 T-GDI 100: deceleration = 27.78^2 / (2 x 35.5) = 10.87 m/s^2, so mu >= 10.87 / 9.781 = 1.11, rounded to 1.1 (search snippet only, not opened).

No opened source: a search snippet of a MATEC 2019 paper says passenger-car tyres on smooth asphalt range 0.007 to 0.02 with 0.012 cited most often; 0.012 is the owner's choice until the paper is opened.
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification rates the Kia Rio 1.25 MPI at 84 ps (62 kW) at 6,000 rpm (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification rates the Kia Rio 1.25 MPI at 122 Nm at 4,000 rpm (search snippet only, not opened).

Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification lists the Kia Rio 1.25 MPI five-speed manual at 3.545, 1.895, 1.192 (seen in three snippets) and about 0.906, 0.719 (one garbled snippet); the 0.72 top gear matches Carfolio's Hyundai i20 1.2 84 PS (search snippets only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Irish launch release for the Kia Rio lists reverse 3.636 for the 1.25 MPI in one snippet and 3.583 in another; 3.636 is taken and must be checked (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Irish launch release for the Kia Rio lists a 4.600 final drive for the 1.25 MPI manual, matching Carfolio's 4.60 for the Hyundai i20 1.2 84 PS (search snippet only, not opened).
No maker figure was found; a MotorBeam road test snippet says a related 1.2 Kappa engine 'redlines just above 6500 RPM'; 6,500 rpm is the owner's choice, proposed, not sourced for this engine.

No opened source: a search snippet of an MDPI World Electric Vehicle Journal paper puts manual transmission efficiency at 92-97 % and uses 0.92 as a worst case; 0.92 is the owner's choice until the paper is opened.
The owner's choice (orchestrator decision E1(a)), proposed 0.3 s; no source exists, so the url is a placeholder that names no source.

No Kia figure found; median of three published values for peer cars: Suzuki Swift 2017 0.32 (Auto Express table), Hyundai i20 1.2 0.30 (Carfolio), Kia Rio 1.4 2017 0.32 (automobile-catalog estimate) (search snippets only, not opened).
No opened source for the factor: the EcoModder wiki snippet gives frontal area as width x height x 0.84; 0.84 x 1.725 x 1.450 = 2.10 m^2 is the owner's choice until a textbook source is opened.

No opened source: a search snippet of a University of Michigan traction/braking paper gives an optimal 69/31 front/rear split on a dry road (mu 0.85) for one vehicle model; 0.7 is the owner's choice until the paper is opened.
ADAC's braking test is from 100 km/h (27.78 m/s) (search snippet only, not opened).

ADAC measured 35.5 m from 100 km/h for a Kia Rio 1.0 T-GDI 100 (same YB body, different engine); auto motor und sport measured 37.1 m and 35.8 m on two 1.0 T-GDI 120 cars (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification quotes acceleration 0-100 km/h (27.78 m/s) (search snippet only, not opened).
Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification gives the Kia Rio 1.25 MPI 0-100 km/h in 12.9 s; ADAC's catalogue repeats it (search snippet only, not opened).

Kia's 2017 Rio European technical specification and Irish release give the Kia Rio 1.25 MPI a top speed of 170 km/h (47.22 m/s); ADAC's German catalogue lists 173 km/h (search snippet only, not opened).
